newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Santer congratulates Blair on victory.
newsitem.headline: EU's Santer congratulates Blair on victory.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer congratulated British Labour leader Tony Blair on his election as British Prime Minister on Friday and said he wanted to meet him as soon as possible.
"It's an outstanding victory for the Labour Party," he told Reuters Television. "We are looking forward to working very closely with the government."
He urged the incoming Labour government to give Britain in Europe "a great role corresponding to its great history and its experience."
Santer said in a telegram to Blair he hoped to meet him soon, in view of the challenges facing the 15-nation Union.

The landslide victory of Blair's Labour Party in Thursday's General Election comes in the crucial closing stages of the EU inter-governmental conference which is overhauling the EU treaties, to prepare the bloc for expansion to up to 12 new members.
The conference is set to wind up at the EU's June 16-17 Amsterdam Summit, preceded by a special summit in the Dutch coastal town of Noordwijk on May 23.
Santer also pointed out that Britain would take over the presidency of the EU in the first half of next year.
"Never more than now has the European Union needed strong British commitment with its unique combination of pragmatism and efficiency," his telegram said.
Santer told Reuters Television he had never attempted to interfere in the British election campaign.
British media had interpreted a recent speech in which he condemned Eurosceptic attitudes in Europe as an attack on the Conservative government, whose campaign was dogged by a split over Europe.
Ireland's European Commissioner Padraig Flynn said in a statement he that he was glad that all EU members would now be able to subscribe to EU social policy.
Blair has already indicated that he will sign up to the social protocol of the Maastricht Treaty, something the previous John Major government had always steadfastly refused to do.

"I am very pleased that we will soon return to the position where all member states subscribe to the promotion of a social Europe. I believe, and this is a view endorsed by the Commission, that there should be a common base for social rights for all the people in the European Union," Flynn said.
The President of the European Parliament, Jose-Maria Gil Robles, said in a statement said the EU assembly looked forward to a close working relationship with Blair during the British EU presidency.
